comments.title: Ignore negated stop phrases
comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Ignore negated stop phrases**

If the user says something like `N'arrête pas cstack` or `don't stop cstack`, `STOP.search(prompt)` still matches `arrête`/`stop` followed by `cstack`, so this branch deletes the session marker despite the user explicitly asking to keep the mode active. Subsequent turns then receive no reminder; stop detection should distinguish affirmative requests from common negated forms.

comments.title: Scope activation refusals to cstack
comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Scope activation refusals to cstack**

When an explicit invocation also contains an unrelated prohibition such as `$cstack:cstack fix this, but do not activate debug mode`, the bare `do not activate` alternative matches even though it does not refer to cstack. The hook therefore creates no session marker and omits reminders on later prompts or resumes despite the explicit invocation; require the refusal to name `it` or `cstack`, as the `use`/`invoke` alternatives already do.

comments.title: Keep explicit “this skill” refusals inactive
comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep explicit “this skill” refusals inactive**

When the prompt explicitly says `$cstack:cstack Explain it, but do not activate this skill`, the narrowed English branch no longer matches because it accepts only `it`, `cstack`, or the literal command after `activate`; `_activation_requested` consequently returns true and persists cstack mode despite the user's refusal. The previous expression recognized this `do not activate` form, so the target-aware matcher should also recognize unambiguous noun phrases such as `this/the cstack skill`.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L7-L7](https://github.com/charlescstpierr/cstack/blob/f16ad37e081e615c932be24702faf4d38b77f06b/AGENTS.md#L7-L7)

comments.title: Recognize infinitive French activation refusals
comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Recognize infinitive French activation refusals**

Although the updated matcher now covers the previously missed English `this skill` form, the new French branch still misses the common infinitive construction `$cstack:cstack explique la compétence, mais ne pas activer cstack`: it requires `pas` after the `activ...` verb, so `_activation_requested` returns true and persists cstack mode despite the explicit refusal. Accept `ne pas activer/utiliser/appliquer cstack` alongside the finite forms.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L7-L7](https://github.com/charlescstpierr/cstack/blob/e41552f324fdf0b0f2521a85c7ade177827d03f2/AGENTS.md#L7-L7)

comments.title: Ignore quoted refusal text after an explicit invocation
comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Ignore quoted refusal text after an explicit invocation**

When an explicitly invoked task asks to write or test refusal text—for example, `$cstack:cstack Ajoute au README la phrase « ne pas utiliser cstack »`—the new suffix-wide alternative matches the quoted phrase and returns `False`, so the session marker and reminder are never created despite the explicit invocation. Exclude quoted/code spans from refusal detection, or otherwise require the negation to be an instruction rather than requested content.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L7-L7](https://github.com/charlescstpierr/cstack/blob/98427161bbb182aacafece037fed610291eaf3a6/AGENTS.md#L7-L7)

comments.title: Exclude Markdown blockquotes from refusal detection
comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Exclude Markdown blockquotes from refusal detection**

The current quote-stripping fix still leaves Markdown blockquote bodies in the instruction text, so an explicitly invoked prompt such as `$cstack:cstack Explain this example:\n> Do not activate cstack` is classified as a refusal and never creates the session marker. This is fresh evidence beyond the earlier quoted-string case: the new regex handles delimiter-based quotes and code spans but not the standard `>` quotation form. Strip blockquoted content before applying the refusal regex.
